chapter_theme: Three songs at Thanjai (தஞ்சை): a short plea not to wander in women's maya, a plea to end the illusion and be given the true substance that is everywhere, and a courtesan scene with a plea for knowledge; the praise names Murugan as Siva's teacher and the great towered city.
structure_note: 883 is a short song; 884 asks for the pervading truth; 885 is a courtesan catalogue.

883.reading: A short song: the poet asks whether he will wander in the maya of women with kohl-dark spear eyes, and whether grace will not come in visible form so that he may reach Murugan's feet. The praise names him the son of Hara who ate poison as nectar and of Uma, dwelling at Thanjai so that devotees who take refuge may live.
883.nuance: தஞ்சென ... தஞ்சையில்: a pun on the place name and தஞ்சம், refuge. விம்பமதாய் அருள் may mean grace taking an image or form; the sense is not certain.

884.reading: The poet confesses that in the wish to sink in the sea of pleasure with women whose eyes are like kendai fish hiding in the sea, he left off thinking of Murugan, and asks that, to end this conjuror's illusion, Murugan call him kindly 'come here' and give the true substance that is everywhere. The praise names Valli with her twig-waist and cloud-dark hair, Murugan the teacher of Sambhu whose fire-eye killed Kama, and the lord of great Thanjai with its towering gopuram and golden mansions.
884.nuance: இந்த்ரசால இப்ப்ரமை: the world of desire is a magic show (indrajala) and a delusion. எங்குமான மெய்ப்பொருள் தாராய்: the remedy is the pervading reality, given by the call 'come here' (எங்கு வா). சம்பராரியைக் கொன்ற தீவிழிச் சம்பு போதகக் குருநாதா: Murugan as guru to Siva who burned Kama.

885.reading: The poet describes courtesans who comb their hair, smear turmeric, wear pearls, draw in everyone they see on the street, bare their breasts, throw the spears of their eyes, name a price and take those who come to bed, and asks that the evil deeds and births of pleasure with them fade away, that Murugan give the knowledge of jnana and come with his kadamba garland. The praise names Vishnu who brought Indra's tree to earth, the conch-bearer Kesava, as uncle, the vel that dusted Taraka's armies in the eight directions, Parvati, moon-crowned, serpent-adorned, who swallowed the poison, as the mother who gave Murugan, and the lord on the peacock at the royal gopuram of great Thanjai.
885.nuance: விலைகூறி: the price is named. அநுபோக தீவினைப் பவங்கள்: the pleasures are counted as evil deeds that make births, and the cure asked is ஞான வித்தை. இந்த்ர தாருவை ஞாலமீதினிற் கொணர்ந்த is Krishna bringing the parijata tree. தஞ்சைமாநகர் ராஜகோபுரம்: the great gopuram of Thanjavur.
